title: Vote: recommend a standard User-Agent format for REST clients
summary: rahul mahadev called a vote on standardizing the client User-Agent format in the REST catalog spec (PR #17727), following a discussion thread. A +1 endorses that clients identify themselves with the standard HTTP User-Agent header as whitespace-separated product/version tokens, most specific first (engine, integration or connector, Iceberg library, runtime), with an optional parenthesized comment; that the Iceberg library token must be present when the header is sent; and that the header is advisory, so servers must not reject requests for a missing or malformed header or use it for authentication, though they may refuse client versions known to be unsafe. It is not a capability negotiation mechanism. Three non-binding +1 votes followed. Alex Dutra then said he had posted more comments on the PR that should be addressed before proceeding. No result is stated in the thread.

positions.stance: Adopt an advisory, RFC 7231 style User-Agent format in the REST spec that always includes the Iceberg library token.
Supports the advisory format, kept separate from authentication and capability negotiation and tolerant of clients that omit the header.
Further comments on the PR should be addressed before the vote proceeds.

outcome.note: No result is stated. The thread has 3 non-binding +1 votes and a request to address further PR comments before proceeding.

why_it_matters: If adopted, the Java, Python, Rust and Go clients would be changed to emit the same User-Agent format.
